findings.reason: Lock fs_enet_private.tx_lock is shared between softirq-context and process-context code with the process side missing bottom-half disable (exact seed shape). UNTRUSTED TRIGGER: any packet or event that runs the driver's NAPI poll under NET_RX softirq or ndo_start_xmit under NET_TX softirq, plus any device close (ifconfig down). SOFTIRQ SIDE: fs_enet_interrupt (request_irq at fs_enet-main.c:733) -> napi_schedule_prep/__napi_schedule (lines 344/352) -> fs_enet_napi (NAPI poll, line 86) takes the SAME fep->tx_lock with plain spin_lock at line 99 and reaps TX descriptors; additionally fs_enet_start_xmit (ndo_start_xmit, netdev_ops line 897) takes the same plain spin_lock at line 523 in NET_TX softirq context. PROCESS SIDE: fs_enet_close (line 754) calls netif_stop_queue (758) and napi_disable(&fep->napi) (761), then takes spin_lock_irqsave(&fep->lock) at 764 and plain spin_lock(&fep->tx_lock) at 765. The outer spin_lock_irqsave disables hard interrupts on the local CPU but does NOT disable bottom halves, and there is no spin_lock_bh/local_bh_disable anywhere in the file (rg 'spin_lock_bh' = 0 hits in fs_enet-main.c). A NET_TX/NET_RX softirq that runs on the same CPU while fs_enet_close holds tx_lock (between 765 and 767, including the ->stop hardware quiesce which is slow register access) spins on tx_lock forever while the holder can never resume, the exact self-deadlock the seed patch fixed with spin_lock_bh. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: napi_disable() at 761 does synchronize with an in-flight fs_enet_napi poll, and netif_stop_queue at 758 stops new xmits, which narrows the window; however the window is not closed: the IRQ remains requested (free_irq comes later at 772), so fs_enet_interrupt can still run and __napi_schedule a new poll, and an already-running fs_enet_start_xmit (plain spin_lock at 523) on another queue path or a poll that raced just after napi_disable's grace window can be dispatched as a softirq on the close-holding CPU. Reported as a medium-confidence hypothesis: static pairing is proven (same lock object, plain acquisition on both sides, zero BH-disable anywhere in the file), runtime reproduction was not performed.

findings.reason: Lock cas.tx_lock[] is shared between softirq-context TX-completion code and process/workqueue-context code with the process side missing bottom-half disable. SOFTIRQ SIDE: cas_poll (NAPI poll, scheduled from cas_interrupt/cas_interruptN/cas_interrupt1 hardirq handlers via napi_schedule at lines 2462/2513/2569) -> cas_tx (line 1927) -> cas_tx_ringN takes spin_lock(&cp->tx_lock[ring]) with plain spin_lock at line 1862 (unlock 1924); cas_interrupt hardirq itself also calls cas_tx directly at line 2562. PROCESS SIDE: cas_reset_task (workqueue worker, line 4005, scheduled from cas_tx_timeout at 2721, cas_abnormal_irq at 2740/2740b, and link handling at 1829/1833/3879/3884) calls cas_lock_all_save (line 4032) which does spin_lock_irq(&cp->lock) then cas_lock_tx (line 249) acquiring every tx_lock with plain spin_lock_nested - hard interrupts are excluded but bottom halves are NOT disabled; cas_open (4256) and cas_close (4295) and the link-reset path (cas_link_reset, cas_lock_tx at 4103) use the same helpers. The xmit path itself (cas_xmit_tx_ringN, line 2775) correctly uses spin_lock_irqsave, which proves the driver knows the xmit side runs with IRQs/BH active, yet the workqueue/open/close/link-reset side only disables IRQs, not BH. A NET_RX/NET_TX softirq on the same CPU while the reset worker holds tx_lock[ring] spins forever on that lock (cas_poll/cas_tx_ringN) while the preempted worker can never resume -> soft lockup / RCU stall / TX stall DoS, the exact seed mechanism. COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: cas_reset_task first calls netif_device_detach(cp->dev) (line 4030) before taking locks, which discourages new xmits, but NAPI polls already scheduled by the hardirq are not quiesced (no napi_disable in the reset path; cas_close does napi_disable before locking but cas_open's request_irq precedes later locking sections and cas_poll runs as softirq); no spin_lock_bh exists anywhere in cassini.c (rg count 0). Reported as a medium-confidence hypothesis: static lock-context pairing is proven, runtime reproduction was not performed.

cas_tx_ringN plain spin_lock(&cp->tx_lock[ring]) reachable from NAPI poll (cas_poll -> cas_tx) and hardirq, while workqueue cas_reset_task/open/close/link-reset take the same tx_lock via cas_lock_tx (plain spin_lock_nested, line 249) under only spin_lock_irq(&cp->lock) - IRQs disabled, BH not; no spin_lock_bh in the file.

limitations: Search bounded to snapshot s06 only, as required; other snapshots were not inspected.

Static analysis only: lock-context pairing was established by source reading; no runtime reproduction, lockdep run, or compilation was performed, so both findings remain hypotheses about exploitability.

For fs_enet, napi_disable() at line 761 and netif_stop_queue at 758 narrow the close-path window substantially; the finding depends on the residual window (free_irq at 772 happens later, so fs_enet_interrupt can still schedule a new NAPI poll, and in-flight xmit under NET_TX softirq at line 523 is only discouraged, not synchronized, by netif_stop_queue).

For cassini, cas_reset_task calls netif_device_detach before taking locks, which reduces but does not eliminate softirq-side contention (NAPI polls already scheduled are not quiesced by netif_device_detach; the driver has no napi_disable in the reset path).

Candidate ranking covered drivers/net and drivers/staging files that define ndo_start_xmit/hard_start_xmit (441 files) and were filtered by plain spin_lock presence; the top unresolved entries (altera_tse, forcedeth, sbni, cris/eth_v10, and mid-ranked files like mvneta, ixgbe, igb, cpmac, ravb, team, rionet) were not per-site attributed before the finalize deadline.
drivers outside net/ (e.g., non-net spinlock users reachable from softirq) were not enumerated for this branch.
